transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before I sign Thursday's airlift manifest, I need to confirm whether operations, signal, and medical have any changes to their standard pallet requests. As a reminder, the contracted aircraft has capacity for exactly 23 pallets, and our normal weekly request totals 18 pallets — 8 engineering, 5 communications batteries, and 5 medical supplies — leaving 5 unused spaces. If anyone has changes to their requirements, please report them now so I can finalize the manifest and loading instructions.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Major. Operations has a change to report. I confirmed this morning that the engineering detachment's work order was moved ahead by the receiving site and now requires exactly 10 engineering pallets — two above our normal request of 8. This revised work order has not yet been entered on the airlift manifest.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good morning, Major. Signal has a change to report. I confirmed with the aircrew loadmaster that the communications battery shipment is now exactly 7 pallets — two above our normal request of 5. Additionally, the loadmaster specified that the communications battery pallets must be loaded first for the aircraft's pallet-restraint inspection. This update is not yet on the battalion briefing slide.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Good morning, Major. Medical has a change to report. I confirmed that the receiving clinic's resupply order requires exactly 6 medical-supply pallets — one above our normal request of 5 — because the clinic's cold-storage replenishment was advanced to Thursday. The revised order is still being reconciled with the medical warehouse ledger.
transcript.speaker: A4
